episodes.title_zh: 吸管裡的飲料是誰推上去的？
episodes.question: What really lifts a drink through a straw?
invariants: Open cup and submerged straw; no pressure arrows pulling upward from mouth. Downward pressure at exposed surface; upward displacement in tube after pressure difference.
Same room pressure throughout. Compare relative air pressure labels only; no absolute values or identical force arrows across differently sized surfaces.
At release show liquid fall back only after tube opens to room air.
episodes.simplification: Neglect capillary rise in a typical drinking straw and flow losses; drawn markers are qualitative.
episodes.description_en: Lowering air pressure above the liquid in a straw lets the relatively greater atmospheric pressure acting on the drink surface push liquid up the straw.
episodes.description_zh: 讓外面的空氣重新進入管口，飲料就會落回杯中液面的高度。

sources.evidence: Drinking-from-a-straw example, lines 162–164: pressure difference and outside pressure pushing liquid.
Sucking Water Through a Straw: mouth pressure decreases and surrounding air pushes on liquid.

claims.text: Lowering air pressure above the liquid in a straw lets the relatively greater atmospheric pressure acting on the drink surface push liquid up the straw.

cues.en: Watch this drink climb a straw. Where does the push really come from?
cues.zh: 飲料會沿著吸管往上爬。到底是誰在推？
cues.visual: Macro cutaway of open cup and striped straw; liquid rises, then freeze above the cup’s surface.

cues.en: Before the sip, the straw is open and room air reaches both surfaces.
cues.zh: 喝之前，吸管開著，管內外的液面都接觸室內空氣。
cues.visual: Pull back to a cross section with an open upper end and two equal-level menisci; label both room pressure.

cues.en: Now seal your lips around the straw and draw some air out of it.
cues.zh: 嘴唇包緊吸管，先把管裡一些空氣吸出來。
cues.visual: Close-up at mouth end; animate a few schematic air markers departing that end.

cues.en: That makes the air pressure inside the straw lower than the pressure outside.
cues.zh: 吸管裡的氣壓，就比外面低了。
cues.visual: Split inset of air above tube and cup; show lower vs room pressure with comparison labels.

cues.en: Room air still presses on the exposed drink surface. That pressure pushes liquid up the straw.
cues.zh: 外面的空氣還在壓著杯中液面，於是把飲料推上吸管。
cues.visual: Return to cup cross-section; downward arrows above exposed surface, then animate liquid rising in the connected column.

cues.en: The difference in pressure is what gets the liquid moving upward against gravity.
cues.zh: 正是內外氣壓的差，讓液體能逆著重力往上。
cues.visual: Track the moving meniscus; retain lower-pressure label above it and a small downward gravity marker off to the side.

cues.en: Open the top to room air again, and the liquid drops back to the cup’s level.
cues.zh: 讓外面的空氣重新進入管口，飲料就會落回杯中液面的高度。
cues.visual: Pull back as mouth lifts away; equalize pressure indicators first, then settle both surfaces at the same height.

visual_plan.action: Macro cutaway of open cup and striped straw; liquid rises, then freeze above the cup’s surface.
Pull back to a cross section with an open upper end and two equal-level menisci; label both room pressure.
Close-up at mouth end; animate a few schematic air markers departing that end.
Split inset of air above tube and cup; show lower vs room pressure with comparison labels.
Return to cup cross-section; downward arrows above exposed surface, then animate liquid rising in the connected column.
Track the moving meniscus; retain lower-pressure label above it and a small downward gravity marker off to the side.
Pull back as mouth lifts away; equalize pressure indicators first, then settle both surfaces at the same height.

episodes.title_zh: 倒水後，硬幣為什麼又出現？
episodes.question: Why can you see a coin after adding water without moving the coin or your eye?
invariants: Keep eye, coin, cup and rim fixed in both views.
Trace physical rays from coin toward eye, kink at water-air surface only; outgoing angle from vertical normal is larger than incoming angle, below critical incidence.
Opaque cup. After refraction, path clears the near rim; before water, straight coin-eye path strikes the rim.
episodes.simplification: Use a representative ray per view. No total internal reflection, glare, waves, or measuring optical angles.
episodes.description_en: With fixed coin and eye positions, adding water creates a water-air boundary. A light ray from the coin can refract away from the normal and reach the eye over the cup rim.
episodes.description_zh: 水改變了光走的路，硬幣還是在原本的地方。

sources.publisher: University of Iowa Physics and Astronomy
sources.evidence: Penny and Cup lab: line of sight blocked by rim before filling and penny appears after filling.
Re-appearing penny demonstration: refraction at the water surface changes which rays reach the viewer.

claims.text: With fixed coin and eye positions, adding water creates a water-air boundary. A light ray from the coin can refract away from the normal and reach the eye over the cup rim.

cues.en: This coin vanishes behind a cup rim. Add water, and it appears again.
cues.zh: 硬幣被杯緣擋住了。倒點水，它卻又出現。
cues.visual: Use fixed eye-level view of a cup. Coin invisible in the empty view, reveal only once the water settles.

cues.en: The coin stays at the bottom, and your eye stays in exactly the same spot.
cues.zh: 硬幣留在杯底，你的眼睛也停在原處。
cues.visual: Show a cutaway side view with lock marks on coin and eye; mark the opaque near rim.

cues.en: In the empty cup, the straight path from the coin to your eye hits the rim.
cues.zh: 杯子空的時候，硬幣到眼睛的直線路徑會撞上杯緣。
cues.visual: Animate one ray along the straight path and stop it at the opaque rim, leaving a dashed blocked continuation.

cues.en: Once you add water, light from the coin can cross from water into air.
cues.zh: 加水後，來自硬幣的光能從水進入空氣。
cues.visual: Wipe water into cup while retaining coin and eye position; focus the flat water surface.

cues.en: As a ray crosses at an angle, it bends away from a line straight up from the surface.
cues.zh: 光線斜著穿出水面時，會往遠離垂直線的方向偏折。
cues.visual: Zoom at boundary; draw dashed vertical normal and correct incoming/outgoing segments.

cues.en: That bend is refraction. A ray now clears the rim and reaches your eye.
cues.zh: 這叫折射。折過去的光越過杯緣，進到你眼睛裡。
cues.visual: Pull back and animate the full transmitted ray from coin to eye above rim.

cues.en: The water changes the path of the light while the coin sits right where it started.
cues.zh: 水改變了光走的路，硬幣還是在原本的地方。
cues.visual: Match-cut initial and filled eye views against stationary cup and coin schematic.

visual_plan.action: Use fixed eye-level view of a cup. Coin invisible in the empty view, reveal only once the water settles.
Show a cutaway side view with lock marks on coin and eye; mark the opaque near rim.
Animate one ray along the straight path and stop it at the opaque rim, leaving a dashed blocked continuation.
Wipe water into cup while retaining coin and eye position; focus the flat water surface.
Zoom at boundary; draw dashed vertical normal and correct incoming/outgoing segments.
Pull back and animate the full transmitted ray from coin to eye above rim.
Match-cut initial and filled eye views against stationary cup and coin schematic.

episodes.title_en: Why Does Metal Feel Colder Than Wood?
episodes.title_zh: 同樣室溫，金屬為什麼摸起來更冷？
episodes.question: Why does room-temperature metal feel colder than room-temperature wood?
invariants: Equal initial sample temperature, both below skin temperature; identical contact area and start time.
Heat arrows from hands toward both samples, thicker or faster on metal; no cold arrows travelling toward hands.
Changing skin temperature at contact, not changing ambient reading; no numeric rate claim.
episodes.simplification: Focus on transient heat transfer into familiar bulk materials. Actual cooling depends on contact, thermal effusivity, and sample properties.
episodes.description_en: Objects equilibrated in the same room can share a temperature. Common metal in contact with warmer skin typically carries heat away more rapidly than wood, cooling the skin faster and feeling colder.
episodes.description_zh: 兩把尺一開始一樣暖。差別在於它們帶走你手上熱量的速度。

sources.evidence: Getting Warmer/Getting Colder personally compares thermometer readings and heat leaving skin.
Introduction lines 407–417 directly compares room-temperature wood and metal and heat conduction from the hand.

claims.text: Objects equilibrated in the same room can share a temperature. Common metal in contact with warmer skin typically carries heat away more rapidly than wood, cooling the skin faster and feeling colder.

cues.en: Touch this metal ruler, then this wood ruler. Why does one feel colder?
cues.zh: 摸摸金屬尺，再摸木尺。為什麼金屬尺比較冰？
cues.visual: Desk view with metal and wood rulers, separate highlights and fingers entering frame.

cues.en: Both sat on the same desk long enough to reach the same room temperature.
cues.zh: 兩把尺在同一張桌上放了很久，已經到了相同的室溫。
cues.visual: Show paired contact probes with matching qualitative indicators; material textures remain visible.

cues.en: Your fingertips are warmer than either ruler, so heat moves from skin into both.
cues.zh: 指尖比兩把尺都暖，所以熱會從皮膚傳到尺上。
cues.visual: Top-down contact then cross section; same-size contact pads, two arrows pointing from skin into materials.

cues.en: The metal carries that heat away from the contact area faster than the wood.
cues.zh: 金屬比木頭更快把熱從接觸的地方帶走。
cues.visual: Animate equal-size warm highlights spreading quickly into metal and slowly into wood.

cues.en: Heat then keeps leaving the skin more quickly on the metal side.
cues.zh: 因此，碰金屬的那邊，皮膚會繼續更快地失去熱。
cues.visual: Show two qualitative heat-flow arrows of different thickness, both pointing away from skin.

cues.en: That fingertip cools faster, and you feel the difference right at the surface.
cues.zh: 那根手指降溫比較快，摸起來就更冰。
cues.visual: Zoom onto skin pads and show the metal-side skin tone shifting toward cooler color faster.

cues.en: The two rulers started out equally warm. What felt different was how fast they took heat from you.
cues.zh: 兩把尺一開始一樣暖。差別在於它們帶走你手上熱量的速度。
cues.visual: Return to rulers and equal initial thermometer marks; concise takeaway appears.

visual_plan.action: Desk view with metal and wood rulers, separate highlights and fingers entering frame.
Show paired contact probes with matching qualitative indicators; material textures remain visible.
Top-down contact then cross section; same-size contact pads, two arrows pointing from skin into materials.
Animate equal-size warm highlights spreading quickly into metal and slowly into wood.
Show two qualitative heat-flow arrows of different thickness, both pointing away from skin.
Zoom onto skin pads and show the metal-side skin tone shifting toward cooler color faster.
Return to rulers and equal initial thermometer marks; concise takeaway appears.

episodes.question: Why does an isolated, small soap bubble tend to round out after leaving the wand?
invariants: Compare equal enclosed volume in 3D. If shown schematically, use two equal-height width-adjusted silhouettes labelled as slices and avoid equivalent-area/volume claim from 2D outline alone.
Surface tension acts along film, not as independent radial arrows; show short tangential paired pulls or surface-area decrease only.
Bubble free of wand after detaching; no foam clusters or claims all bubbles are perfectly spherical.
episodes.simplification: Assume isolated small bubble in still air. Ignore wind, gravity deformation, film drainage and pressure evolution during detachment.
episodes.description_en: A small free soap bubble is a thin liquid film around air. Surface tension favors less surface area, and for a given enclosed volume a sphere has the least surface area.
episodes.description_zh: 泡泡棒能固定液膜的形狀，自由漂浮的泡泡則會自己變圓。

sources.evidence: Explanation of why free bubbles form spheres and why frames constrain soap films.
Soap bubble formation: surface energy and why the sphere minimizes surface for a fixed volume.

claims.text: A small free soap bubble is a thin liquid film around air. Surface tension favors less surface area, and for a given enclosed volume a sphere has the least surface area.

cues.en: A soap bubble stretches as it leaves the wand. Why does it round out?
cues.zh: 肥皂泡離開泡泡棒時先被拉長，為什麼接著又變圓？
cues.visual: Side-lit backyard scene; soap film stretches on wand briefly then detaches.

cues.en: Look close. The bubble is a thin liquid film wrapped around a pocket of air.
cues.zh: 放大看，肥皂泡是一層很薄的液膜，包住一團空氣。
cues.visual: Magnify one edge, separate colored film from interior air and label as schematic.

cues.en: Making more film surface takes energy, so surface tension favors a smaller surface area.
cues.zh: 增加液膜表面需要能量，所以表面張力會讓表面積傾向縮小。
cues.visual: Inset film patch with two tangent markers, then cut to surface shrink; no force arrows aimed at center.

cues.en: Now compare two shapes holding the same amount of space inside.
cues.zh: 現在比較兩種內部空間一樣大的形狀。
cues.visual: Show an elongated shape and a sphere as 3D outline meshes; label same volume before comparing surfaces.

cues.en: A sphere wraps that volume with the least surface area of any shape.
cues.zh: 相同體積下，球體需要的表面積最小。
cues.visual: Highlight each outer mesh in turn and show the sphere with the shorter qualitative surface-area bar.

cues.en: So once a small bubble floats free, the film tends to settle into a sphere.
cues.zh: 所以，小泡泡自由漂浮後，液膜會趨向球形。
cues.visual: Return to the free bubble, softly damps from elongated to round without shrinking enclosed volume visibly.

cues.en: A wand can hold a film in another shape. A free bubble makes its own round outline.
cues.zh: 泡泡棒能固定液膜的形狀，自由漂浮的泡泡則會自己變圓。
cues.visual: Two final views: stretched film still on the ring versus a separate small round bubble floating.

visual_plan.action: Side-lit backyard scene; soap film stretches on wand briefly then detaches.
Magnify one edge, separate colored film from interior air and label as schematic.
Inset film patch with two tangent markers, then cut to surface shrink; no force arrows aimed at center.
Show an elongated shape and a sphere as 3D outline meshes; label same volume before comparing surfaces.
Highlight each outer mesh in turn and show the sphere with the shorter qualitative surface-area bar.
Return to the free bubble, softly damps from elongated to round without shrinking enclosed volume visibly.
Two final views: stretched film still on the ring versus a separate small round bubble floating.

episodes.title_en: What Makes a Compass Needle Turn?
episodes.title_zh: 指南針的指針是被什麼轉動的？
episodes.question: What causes a freely pivoting compass needle to point near north?
invariants: Keep external field arrows fixed while needle rotates toward them; case may turn independently.
Clearly distinguish geographic map north arrow from local magnetic bearing; no assertion that the needle aims at a single exact point.
Mark tilt restricted by ordinary flat compass, so arrows represent horizontal component.
episodes.simplification: Work with a level compass and a stable local field away from interfering metal or magnets; shown declination exaggerated.
episodes.description_en: A compass needle is a small magnet that pivots to align with the horizontal component of the local magnetic field; Earth’s field normally dominates, but its heading can differ from true north.
episodes.description_zh: 再轉一下外殼。底下的外殼在轉，指針還是跟著磁場方向。

sources.evidence: Needle is a freely pivoting magnet, turns in local or Earth magnetic field, and can have interference.

sources.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
sources.evidence: Compass FAQ explains local horizontal field direction and magnetic declination from true north.

claims.text: A compass needle is a small magnet that pivots to align with the horizontal component of the local magnetic field; Earth’s field normally dominates, but its heading can differ from true north.

cues.en: Turn a compass case. Why does the needle keep swinging back to the same direction?
cues.zh: 轉一下指南針外殼。為什麼指針總會轉回同一個方向？
cues.visual: Compass on trail map; case turns under a still needle after its small wobble.

cues.en: Inside is a tiny magnet balanced on a pivot, so it can turn freely.
cues.zh: 裡面是一根小磁鐵，架在支點上，可以自由轉動。
cues.visual: Exploded side view shows needle balanced on central pin; restore top-down view.

cues.en: Earth produces a magnetic field. Around the compass, that field has a local direction.
cues.zh: 地球有磁場。在指南針所在的位置，磁場有自己的方向。
cues.visual: Pull back from compass to globe with a small selected region, then project back to local schematic.

cues.en: The field twists the needle until it lines up with the field along the ground.
cues.zh: 磁場讓指針轉動，直到它和磁場在水平面上的方向一致。
cues.visual: Side-to-top transition shows tilt projected onto horizontal plane; pivot needle toward fixed arrow.

cues.en: The marked end generally points near map north, but it can be a little off.
cues.zh: 標記的那一端大致朝北，但可能和地圖的正北差一個角度。
cues.visual: Reveal true north first, then local magnetic bearing on same map; small exaggerated angle label.

cues.en: That angle varies from place to place because the field’s direction changes.
cues.zh: 這個角度因地而異，因為各地的磁場方向不同。
cues.visual: Slide between two qualitative map locations with different angle offsets, not numeric values.

cues.en: Turn the case again. The needle follows the field, even while the case turns underneath.
cues.zh: 再轉一下外殼。底下的外殼在轉，指針還是跟著磁場方向。
cues.visual: Back to trail map; animate case markings rotating independently of aligned needle.

visual_plan.action: Compass on trail map; case turns under a still needle after its small wobble.
Exploded side view shows needle balanced on central pin; restore top-down view.
Pull back from compass to globe with a small selected region, then project back to local schematic.
Side-to-top transition shows tilt projected onto horizontal plane; pivot needle toward fixed arrow.
Reveal true north first, then local magnetic bearing on same map; small exaggerated angle label.
Slide between two qualitative map locations with different angle offsets, not numeric values.
Back to trail map; animate case markings rotating independently of aligned needle.

episodes.title_en: Why Does Crumpled Paper Fall Faster?
episodes.title_zh: 同樣的紙，揉成團為什麼掉更快？
episodes.question: Why does a compact paper ball usually beat an identical flat sheet to the ground?
invariants: Use sheets cut from the same stock, same mass, same drop height and start time; no downward shove; air still.
Show equal downward weight arrows, no drag at rest, and compare upward drag at matched falling speed only.
Flat sheet may flutter, so label typical broadside orientation; avoid measured speed or fixed landing gap.
episodes.simplification: Qualitative presentation, no exact trajectories, terminal speed, or Reynolds-number claims.
episodes.description_en: For equal masses, gravitational force is equal; a broadside sheet typically has more upward aerodynamic drag than a compact paper ball at the same falling speed, changing the fall.
episodes.description_zh: 紙一樣，重力也一樣。形狀改變了空氣阻擋下落的程度。

sources.evidence: Flat versus crumpled paper in same gravity; lab changes profile facing air.
Weight and drag directions; drag depends on reference area, speed, density and drag coefficient.

claims.text: For equal masses, gravitational force is equal; a broadside sheet typically has more upward aerodynamic drag than a compact paper ball at the same falling speed, changing the fall.

cues.en: Drop two identical sheets. One is flat. The other is crumpled. Which lands first?
cues.zh: 兩張一樣的紙，一張攤平、一張揉成團。哪張會先落地？
cues.visual: Parallel overhead setup with simultaneous release, pause before either touches floor.

cues.en: Crumpling changes the shape, but you still have the same amount of paper.
cues.zh: 揉紙只改變形狀，紙的份量沒有變。
cues.visual: Quick rewind of one sheet folding itself into a ball; show no scraps and matching mass markers.

cues.en: So gravity pulls down on both with the same force.
cues.zh: 因此，重力往下拉兩張紙的力一樣大。
cues.visual: Show equal downward arrows after reset. Neither sheet has upward drag arrows until moving.

cues.en: As they fall, air pushes back. That opposing force is called drag.
cues.zh: 下落時，空氣會阻擋它們。這個反向的力叫空氣阻力。
cues.visual: Replay falling; upward drag arrows appear only after motion begins.

cues.en: At the same falling speed, the broadside sheet typically meets more air resistance than the compact ball.
cues.zh: 在同樣的下落速度下，攤開迎風的紙通常比紙團受到更大的空氣阻力。
cues.visual: Hold matched-speed demonstration spots, show front-facing silhouettes and qualitative upward drag contrast.

cues.en: The flat sheet flutters and falls more slowly while the ball gets to the floor.
cues.zh: 平紙飄來飄去，下降比較慢，紙團先到了地板。
cues.visual: Return to release view and play a qualitative landing, with flat paper fluttering.

cues.en: Same paper, same gravity. The shape changes how much the air slows the fall.
cues.zh: 紙一樣，重力也一樣。形狀改變了空氣阻擋下落的程度。
cues.visual: End on flat sheet and paper ball in the same frame beside a small airflow cue.

visual_plan.action: Parallel overhead setup with simultaneous release, pause before either touches floor.
Quick rewind of one sheet folding itself into a ball; show no scraps and matching mass markers.
Show equal downward arrows after reset. Neither sheet has upward drag arrows until moving.
Replay falling; upward drag arrows appear only after motion begins.
Hold matched-speed demonstration spots, show front-facing silhouettes and qualitative upward drag contrast.
Return to release view and play a qualitative landing, with flat paper fluttering.
End on flat sheet and paper ball in the same frame beside a small airflow cue.

episodes.title_en: Why Does a Rubbed Balloon Stick to the Wall?
episodes.title_zh: 氣球摩擦過後，為什麼能貼在牆上？
episodes.question: Why can a negatively charged balloon attract and stick to a neutral wall?
invariants: For the rubbed material pair shown, draw equal number of electron tokens moving from cloth to balloon; do not draw protons crossing material boundaries.
Wall remains overall neutral. Show small offsets of bound negative charge away from balloon; positive centers fixed. No long-range electron migration across an insulating wall.
Position wall at one constant side; force toward wall is horizontal and friction acts upward alongside downward weight.
episodes.simplification: Schematic insulator polarization and dry, clean indoor wall. Charge retention and contact friction vary with surface and humidity.
episodes.description_en: Electrons transferred onto a rubbed balloon can give it an excess negative charge. Its electric field polarizes a nearby neutral wall, bringing more positive charge nearer the balloon than negative charge and producing net attraction. At contact, friction can resist downward sliding.
episodes.description_zh: 整面牆的總電荷沒變，變的是電荷的位置。

sources.evidence: Balloon and wall simulation in Step 7 shows electrons transfer to balloon and a neutral wall is attracted after charge separation.
Section 5.2, Polarization: insulator charge shifts by a small amount; neutral objects can be attracted by a nearby charged object.

claims.text: Electrons transferred onto a rubbed balloon can give it an excess negative charge. Its electric field polarizes a nearby neutral wall, bringing more positive charge nearer the balloon than negative charge and producing net attraction. At contact, friction can resist downward sliding.

cues.en: Rub a balloon on a sweater, then let go beside a wall. Why does it stick?
cues.zh: 拿氣球在毛衣上摩擦，再靠著牆放手。為什麼它黏得住？
cues.visual: Cozy room; hand rubs balloon on sweater then opens as balloon hangs against flat wall.

cues.en: Rubbing can move electrons from the sweater onto the balloon, leaving the balloon negatively charged.
cues.zh: 摩擦時，有些電子會從毛衣轉到氣球，讓氣球帶負電。
cues.visual: Magnify fabric and rubber seam, then transfer identical negative tokens from sweater to balloon.

cues.en: As the balloon approaches the wall, its extra electrons repel negative charges in the wall.
cues.zh: 氣球靠近時，多出的電子會排斥牆裡的負電荷。
cues.visual: Pan from charged balloon toward the still-neutral wall and show small charge-pair markers.

cues.en: Those charges shift a tiny bit, leaving positive charge slightly closer to the balloon.
cues.zh: 牆裡的負電荷稍微偏開，正電荷就相對離氣球近一點。
cues.visual: Magnify charge pairs in the wall; keep positive centers fixed and bound negative sides shift by a tiny amount.

cues.en: The closer attraction wins over the farther repulsion, so the wall pulls the balloon in.
cues.zh: 近處的吸引比遠處的排斥強，牆就把氣球吸了過去。
cues.visual: Two opposing force arrows on balloon, larger toward wall; switch to one net attraction arrow.

cues.en: Once they touch, friction at the wall can keep the balloon from sliding down.
cues.zh: 碰到牆之後，摩擦力就能讓氣球不往下滑。
cues.visual: Show vertical wall contact with a small upward friction arrow and the balloon weight downward.

cues.en: The wall stayed neutral overall. What changed was where its charges sat.
cues.zh: 整面牆的總電荷沒變，變的是電荷的位置。
cues.visual: Pull out to balloon on wall. Keep equal count of wall plus and minus glyphs in a schematic inset.

visual_plan.action: Cozy room; hand rubs balloon on sweater then opens as balloon hangs against flat wall.
Magnify fabric and rubber seam, then transfer identical negative tokens from sweater to balloon.
Pan from charged balloon toward the still-neutral wall and show small charge-pair markers.
Magnify charge pairs in the wall; keep positive centers fixed and bound negative sides shift by a tiny amount.
Two opposing force arrows on balloon, larger toward wall; switch to one net attraction arrow.
Show vertical wall contact with a small upward friction arrow and the balloon weight downward.
Pull out to balloon on wall. Keep equal count of wall plus and minus glyphs in a schematic inset.

episodes.title_en: Where Do the Drops on a Cold Glass Come From?
episodes.title_zh: 冰杯外面的水珠是哪來的？
episodes.question: Where does the water on the outside of an intact cold glass come from?
invariants: Water vapor markers only outside the glass; none crosses the intact wall and inside liquid does not color outside droplets.
Temperature arrow falls below a qualitative local dew-point line, not a single universal temperature.
Use equal intact containers in the same room, clean and initially dry; the warm control is above that room’s dew point.
episodes.simplification: No rates, timing guarantees, surface chemistry or fluid-flow model. The outside gas shown is a schematic zoom; water vapor is invisible.
episodes.description_en: Water vapor from the surrounding air can form liquid droplets on the outside of a cold glass when air near the surface is cooled below its dew point.
episodes.description_zh: 這些水珠就是凝結。冰冷的杯壁提供了水蒸氣變成液體的地方。

sources.evidence: Sweatin' to the Coldies: compares outside condensation on cold and room-temperature glass and explains vapor in surrounding air cooling.
Dew Point section lines 1993–2004: droplets form outside a cold glass as ambient water vapor condenses.

claims.text: Water vapor from the surrounding air can form liquid droplets on the outside of a cold glass when air near the surface is cooled below its dew point.

cues.en: A dry glass fills with a cold drink. Tiny drops appear outside. Did it leak?
cues.zh: 乾杯一倒進冰飲，外面就開始冒水珠。是杯子漏水嗎？
cues.visual: Kitchen macro view of an intact tumbler; orange drink inside, clear droplets appear outside.
cues.overlay_en: Where do the drops come from?

cues.en: Look at the air around the glass. It contains water vapor you cannot see.
cues.zh: 看看杯子旁邊的空氣。裡面有看不見的水蒸氣。
cues.visual: Magnify outside air; introduce tiny schematic water vapor markers, never mist or real visible vapor.

cues.en: The cold glass cools the thin layer of air right next to its outside surface.
cues.zh: 冰冷的玻璃，把緊貼在外壁的那一層空氣冷卻。
cues.visual: Cross section shows a cooler color spreading outward from the wall into the thin near-surface region.
cues.overlay_en: Cooler air next to the glass

cues.en: If that air cools below its dew point, some of its water vapor turns into liquid.
cues.zh: 那層空氣低於露點後，部分水蒸氣就會凝結成液態水。
cues.visual: Qualitative thermometer crosses a horizontal dew-point marker; release a few vapor markers toward an outer-surface water drop.

cues.en: That liquid forms droplets on the outside. The water came from the room air.
cues.zh: 液滴在杯外形成。這些水來自房間裡的空氣。
cues.visual: Animate droplets growing on the outside and coalescing; hold an intact wall between orange drink and clear droplets.

cues.en: Set a room-temperature glass next to it. That glass can stay dry in the same room.
cues.zh: 旁邊放一個室溫杯。在同一個房間裡，室溫杯可以維持乾燥。
cues.visual: Two same-shape glasses side by side, one below and one above shown dew-point marker.

cues.en: Those beads are condensation. The cold glass gave water vapor a place to turn liquid.
cues.zh: 這些水珠就是凝結。冰冷的杯壁提供了水蒸氣變成液體的地方。
cues.visual: Back to full tumbler. One outside droplet rolls down while the colored drink stays inside.

episodes.title_en: Why Does a Longer Wrench Help?
episodes.title_zh: 扳手長一點，螺帽為什麼更好轉？
episodes.question: Why does pushing perpendicular to a longer wrench produce more torque on the same nut?
invariants: Same nut axis, arrow lengths, force angle, plane of rotation and drive direction for position comparison.
Arcs indicating torque share same turning sign and are distinguishable from translational force arrows.
End-on push must point through axis of nut and produce no turning torque about its center. No directions to modify a torque-rated wrench.
episodes.simplification: Qualitative demonstration with rigid wrench and fixed pivot. Static friction at the nut controls when it turns and is not quantified.
episodes.description_en: Torque about the nut increases with perpendicular lever arm for the same applied force; with equal perpendicular pushes, applying farther from the nut produces greater turning effect.
episodes.description_zh: 回到側面推。同樣大的力，離轉軸越遠，轉動效果越大。

sources.evidence: Section 10.6: torque about a pivot is force times perpendicular lever arm; direction and point of application both matter.

sources.publisher: UC Santa Barbara Physics Lecture Demonstrations
sources.evidence: Wrenches and screwdrivers: at a right angle torque grows as distance from center of nut to applied push increases.

claims.text: Torque about the nut increases with perpendicular lever arm for the same applied force; with equal perpendicular pushes, applying farther from the nut produces greater turning effect.

cues.en: A stubborn nut barely moves. Why can pushing farther down the wrench make it turn?
cues.zh: 螺帽卡得很緊。為什麼手往扳手末端挪一點，就比較好轉？
cues.visual: Macro workshop bench with centered nut; hand tries a sideways push close to the head.
cues.overlay_en: Why does a longer wrench help?

cues.en: The wrench turns around the center of the nut. Mark that point as the pivot.
cues.zh: 扳手繞著螺帽中心轉。把中心標成轉軸。
cues.visual: Snap to plan view, reveal center target while ruler-like handle remains horizontal.

cues.en: A sideways push makes a turning effect called torque.
cues.zh: 往側面推會產生轉動的效果，叫做扭矩。
cues.visual: One straight force arrow crossing handle at 90 degrees, with separate direction arc by nut.

cues.en: Now use the same sideways push, but put your hand farther from the pivot.
cues.zh: 現在用一樣大的力往側面推，但手移到離轉軸更遠的位置。
cues.visual: Compare near and far push with same straight force arrows and two clearly marked distances.

cues.en: The larger distance gives the same push more torque around the nut.
cues.zh: 距離更大，同樣的力就能在螺帽上產生更大的扭矩。
cues.visual: Animated larger arc or qualitative torque bars; still show both equal force arrows.

cues.en: Push straight along the handle instead, and the force points through the pivot without turning it.
cues.zh: 如果改成沿著握柄推，力就會通過轉軸，不會把螺帽轉動。
cues.visual: Rotate force arrow to point straight along handle through center; turning arc vanishes.

cues.en: Back to the sideways push. Farther out means more turning effect with the same force.
cues.zh: 回到側面推。同樣大的力，離轉軸越遠，轉動效果越大。
cues.visual: Return to workshop view; hand moves outward and the nut gives a short clear turn.
